title: Data Engineering Trends: AI Anxiety and Workflow Orchestration
body_md:
**TL;DR**

- AI agents and software development practices are rising topics of concern.
- Engineers are debating the long-term impact of AI on job security.
- Performance optimization remains a priority for Databricks and Apache Iceberg users.
- Workflow orchestration tools are evolving beyond simple job scheduling.

The role of AI agents and the broader implications for software development are currently top-of-mind for data engineers. Discussions reflect a growing anxiety regarding the future of the profession, with many questioning how AI automation and agents will reshape architecture and pipeline management. This uncertainty is driving a deeper focus on how engineers can adapt their skill sets as the industry shifts toward more automated, AI-integrated workflows.

Technical performance and platform choices continue to dominate practical discussions. Users are actively benchmarking Apache Iceberg versions for cost optimization and sharing strategies to improve Databricks pipeline efficiency, such as moving away from driver-side orchestration. These efforts highlight a persistent need for granular control over data processing, even as higher-level abstractions become more common.

Workflow orchestration is also seeing renewed interest, with engineers evaluating tools like Airflow, Kestra, and Temporal for production systems. The conversation is moving toward treating orchestration as a core backend component rather than a simple scheduling utility. As the ecosystem matures, developers are looking for platforms that can handle complex, modern data flows while maintaining the flexibility required for diverse technical stacks.
